You receive the task of this run and the TODO comments found in a Python package, one grep match per line. Choose the one TODO that fits the task and that a small, local change can resolve, read the surrounding code, and return a plan: the file, the TODO, and the change to make. # Tool instructions

## read

Use read on a directory to inspect its sorted immediate entries. Read a file before editing it, then pass its version to edit as expected_version. Continue from the offset in a truncation notice rather than rereading from the start.

## grep

Use grep to locate definitions, call sites, and strings across the tree before reading whole files. Narrow with glob (for example "*.rs") and set literal when the pattern contains regex metacharacters.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a text file with line numbers or list a directory's immediate entries. Shows at most 2000 lines or 50 KiB per call; when more remains, the result names the offset to continue from. File reads return a sha256 version of the complete bytes. Binary files are reported with their size rather than shown.

limit.description: Maximum lines or entries to show. Default and cap 2000.

offset.description: First line or directory entry to show, 1-indexed. Default 1.

path.description: File or directory path, absolute or relative to the first read root.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a regular expression under a directory or in one file, honoring .gitignore. Matching lines come back sorted by path and line, up to limit (default 100); each line is clamped at 500 characters. The line-search buffer uses at most 8 MiB and stops after 10000 matches or 20000 result lines.

context.description: Lines of context before and after each match. Default 0.

glob.description: Only search files whose path matches this glob, for example "*.py" or "src/**/*.ts".

literal.description: Treat pattern as a fixed string. Default false.

path.description: Directory or file to search. Default: the first read root.

pattern.description: Regular expression (Rust regex syntax), or a literal string when literal is true.

tools.name: return
tools.description: Finish the task by returning its result. The value must conform to the declared schema. A conforming value ends the episode; a value that does not conform is rejected with the reason, and the episode continues.
